consumed.ci-job-structure: one .github/workflows/ci.yml whose jobs are partitioned by whether a check compiles Rust, never by which check it is. Tier 0 is a single always-run detector job named plan on ubuntu-latest carrying no toolchain, no cache action and no target/ directory: after actions/checkout with fetch-depth 0 and persist-credentials false it runs one bash step under set -euo pipefail that computes git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-renames --name-only from BASE_SHA to HEAD, so the path list includes the source side of every rename, with BASE_SHA read from github.event.pull_request.base.sha through the step env block, treats every file name as data and never evaluates it, and writes exactly four job outputs - code, web, workflows, docs - as the literal strings true or false and never as any other value, publishing true on all four for every event whose name is not pull_request so that pushes to main and merge-queue entries are never skip-gated. Every output that gates a required check fails closed, whether the check compiles or not, so a path nobody anticipated runs the gate rather than skipping it, and the body makes that structural - code and web start true and are set false only on affirmative proof that every changed path is skippable, a grep exit of 1, never on a match, an error or a test cut short, and workflows and docs likewise start true and are set false only on a grep exit of 1, and every path test reads the whole list from a here-string rather than through a pipeline whose early-exiting grep can end it under pipefail: code is the negation of a skip-list of paths that cannot affect a compile, a package or an installed artifact, with every entry of the package include allow-list R49 owns forced non-skippable because each of them is a packaging input, and with no skip-list entry allowed to match a file any package contains - so the Markdown entry matches only root-level files. Markdown under docs/ and .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ stays skippable through those directory entries, and no entry matches anything under src/ or a member directory, because src/ is packaged and a workspace member that names no include list packages its whole directory; web is fail-closed too - every change that sets code also sets web, because the web member depends on the core member and the root package that hosts the serve binary depends on every member, and web is additionally set by any change under the web member's directory, so the paths R69 names are a subset of the rule rather than its whole; workflows gates only workflow-lint and its pattern contains the whole input of every check in that job by construction - the workflow files, the local actions they call, which live under .github/actions/, and the workflow linter's own config file; docs keys on the prose tree and gates no job in this file, because R82's link check is a step of hygiene, so it is kept only as a literal output that no check whose input another item declares may consume; and a fifth key is added only when some job would be skipped by it that code does not already skip, and is itself written as the negation of a skip-list, or, if it gates only a job that compiles nothing, as a pattern containing that job's whole input. Tier 1 is the checks that compile nothing, each its own cheap job carrying no cache step: hygiene, which deliberately has no needs edge so that a formatter failure still reports on a pull request whose compile tier is skipped, and which hosts every non-compiling check whose input no key contains, R29's non-code formatting slot and R20's two action-pin checks included, as is R82's link check, while R82's rustdoc part is the doc build step of check; and workflow-lint, gated on workflows, which hosts only checks whose whole input is the workflow tree. Tier 2 is the checks that compile: ONE job named check per entry of target-os-matrix through a strategy matrix over os alone with fail-fast false - never a matrix dimension over Cargo features, because the cache action keys on the job id and not on matrix values - running clippy with the feature off, clippy with the feature on, a no-default-features check of the facade, cargo test with the feature off scoped by -p to the non-web packages so the feature-off property is proven rather than assumed, cargo test over the workspace with the feature on, a build of the serve binary and a doc build, as ordered steps sharing one target/, every cargo command carrying --locked, where each cargo step runs under !cancelled() so that one failing step does not hide the results of the steps after it; plus msrv-floor, a separate single-runner job rather than a matrix leg of check because the floor needs only the declared-floor check Cargo's own CI guide shows rather than check's whole step list, verifying the declared rust-version on ubuntu-latest, which widens to every runner by substituting the matrix os expression into runs-on if the owner answers the open F033 cross-product question that way; plus install-smoke, R50's one ubuntu-latest job, whose web leg is a step conditioned on the web output. Every gated job consumes the detector through needs: plan and a POSITIVE predicate of the form needs.plan.outputs.KEY == 'true', never a negated one, and carrying no status function, so that the platform's implicit success() skips every gated job whenever plan fails or is skipped, under either polarity; the positive form is kept for consistency with R18, R86 and the dorny/paths-filter example, because the one remaining empty-key case, a misspelled output name, is caught by lint on the consumer side and by the detector cases on the producer side, and because a consumer that opts out of skip propagation with always() or !cancelled() must read plan's result, never plan's outputs, as its condition; actionlint type-checks the output name and the needs edge but does NOT reject the negated form, so that rule travels in prose to every consumer rather than being left to lint. A failed plan skips every gated job and skipped is a successful check status, so a failed plan must itself fail a required check; this file hands that constraint on without deciding how it is met: either plan is itself a required check, or an aggregate, if R12 chooses one, includes plan in its needs and treats a failure or cancelled result of plan as failure. ci.yml carries no trigger-level paths or paths-ignore filter of any kind, because a workflow skipped by path filtering leaves its checks Pending and blocks merging while a job skipped by a conditional reports Success; its triggers are pull_request and push restricted to main, plus merge_group so a queue's speculative merge still reports; it declares an empty workflow-level permissions map with a per-job re-grant whose scopes are R08's; and it declares workflow-level concurrency with cancel-in-progress true on a group keyed to the workflow plus the pull-request number, falling back to the commit sha when there is no pull request, so a force-push cancels the superseded pull-request run while consecutive pushes to main never cancel one another and keep populating the cache. This file holds no aggregate required-status job, which is R12's, and no release, secret-scanning, devcontainer or AI-review job, which are separate workflow files. Every further check arrives as a named slot under one rule: a check that compiles nothing is a step of hygiene, or its own cheap job behind a path gate only when that gate's key contains the whole input of every check in the job; a check that compiles what check already compiles is an ordered step of check; and a check needing its own toolchain, its own runner or a target/ it must not share becomes its own job with needs: plan and a positive predicate, counted against a ceiling of roughly six cache-bearing job ids per runner, where the budget arithmetic is the sum over cache-bearing job ids of that job id's runner count. Any single-job workflow file that compiles no Rust, R17's scanner included, lands on ubuntu-latest, because it neither shares nor claims a target/ cache entry and gains nothing from a second runner

principles:
**The shared requirement.** No credential reaches a shared remote from a developer machine without having been scanned. Scanning happens at the earliest cheap point (the commit) and again at the last local point before publication (the push). Every suppression is explicit, reviewable in version control, and no broader than the false positive it suppresses. Source: py's precedent as recorded in the prompt (py `lefthook.yml:73` and `:156`, `.gitleaks.toml:10`, `.gitleaksignore:1`; ledger rows F163–F166, `DIVERGENT`, origin `py-only`), tested against the maintainer's current documentation and against executed behaviour.

**Agreement level: policy plus tool and files.** The scanner is a language-agnostic executable; nothing in Python, TypeScript or Rust changes its cost or behaviour at a git hook. So the evidence supports one shared low-level value across all three repositories, not merely a shared capability:

| Must agree across py, ts, rs | May vary |
|---|---|
| the scanner and its pinned version | the hook manager's syntax for declaring the two jobs (R37) |
| the two command lines | the provisioning mechanism (R42 in rs; py keeps its own installer until its follow-on) |
| the `.gitleaks.toml` content | |
| the `.gitleaksignore` header and entry format | |

ts's absence of any secret scanner is a missing capability, not a justified ecosystem difference (both legs checked the ts checkout: `raw/muse.md:25`, `raw/opus.md:113-115`; **carried**, the ts repository is outside this synthesis's read scope). Changing py and ts is a follow-on project; this decision supplies the rationale in `BASELINE-REVIEW` form below.

| B2 | pre-push covers **every publishable, unpublished commit**: `--no-verify` commits, non-`HEAD` branches, detached `HEAD`, local tags, first push to an empty remote | `git push origin <branch>` of a leaking branch exits non-zero and the remote lacks the ref | `R2f`, `R2g`, `R4d`, `R4e`, `R7b`, `R8` |
| B3 | both tiers **fail closed** | scanner absent from `PATH` blocks the push; missing config exits 1; unknown flag exits 126 | `R10a`–`R10c`, `S9`, `S10` |
| B4 | output **never prints the credential** | the token string is absent from scanner output | `S1c`; every log is redacted |
| B5 | the repository's config **cannot be silently overridden** | with `GITLEAKS_CONFIG` pointing at a permissive file, the line without `--config` passes (exit 0) and the recommended line blocks (exit 1) | `S8a`, `S8b`; precedence documented at `snapshots/gitleaks-README.md:138-139` |

**Architectures compared before any tool** (both legs agree on the outcome; the executed rows are this synthesis's):

| Architecture | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| A. two local tiers + the CI tier R17 owns (py's pattern) | **Recommended** | earliest block (B1) plus pre-publication coverage of bypassed commits (B2); CI remains the backstop for clones that never installed hooks |
| B. pre-push only | Rejected | the secret enters local history; removing it needs a rewrite instead of an unstage |
| C. pre-commit only | Rejected | `--no-verify`, `git am` and cherry-picked commits are never scanned locally; the range tier catches them (`R2f`, `R4d`) |
| D. CI only, or platform push protection | Rejected as the only control | the secret has reached the remote and must be rotated. **Carried:** both legs report that R17 runs TruffleHog with verified-only results, which cannot see a credential that does not verify (`raw/opus.md:200`, `:437-438`) |
| E. TruffleHog at every tier | Rejected for hooks | verification needs network egress on every commit (`raw/muse.md:29`); offline it loses its distinguishing feature. **Carried:** Opus's probe 3 shows it missing a generated private key that gitleaks caught (`raw/opus.md:440-444`); not rerun here |

**The tool.** gitleaks is the most-adopted dedicated scanner (29,499 stars, `SRC9`), its maintainer ships the exact staged-tier hook entry this decision uses (`gitleaks git --pre-commit --redact --staged --verbose`, `SRC15`), its default rule set has 222 rules (`SRC16`), and every behaviour above executed on 8.30.1. **Its maintenance state is `at-risk`, not dormant:** the README opens with "Gitleaks is feature complete. I'm not merging new features into Gitleaks. Future releases will be security patches only. I'm shifting my focus to [Betterleaks]" (`snapshots/gitleaks-README.md:12`, `SRC1`); the newest release is v8.30.1 of 2026-03-21, six months before retrieval (`SRC2`, `SRC3`); the eight newest default-branch commits are Dependabot bumps and their merges (`SRC4`, `SRC5`). It is not dormant: there are 0 repository security advisories (`SRC6`), security patches are promised, and the binary runs. **Why keep it despite `at-risk`:** the durable asset is the file format, not the binary. Betterleaks, from gitleaks' original author (`snapshots/betterleaks-README.md:7`, `SRC26`), reads `.betterleaks.toml` then `.gitleaks.toml` (`snapshots/betterleaks-root.go:285`, `SRC28`), `.betterleaksignore` then `.gitleaksignore` (`:297`, `SRC29`), and translates legacy allowlists (`snapshots/betterleaks-translate_filters.go:20`, `SRC30`). A template that writes gitleaks-format files therefore keeps a one-pin switch; the reverse does not hold. Betterleaks is not the pick today because it is 7.7 months old (created 2026-02-03, `SRC23`), changed its filter language from CEL to Expr within that time (`snapshots/betterleaks-README.md:92`, `SRC27`), and could not be executed here (release assets are not a named endpoint). A frozen gitleaks command line and rule set suits a template that ships exact command lines; the cost is that no new token formats arrive after 2026-03-21, which the re-verify trigger bounds.

**The pre-push range.** py's shape resolves a base (`@{u}`, else `origin/HEAD`, else `origin/main`, else warn and exit 0) and scans `<base>..HEAD`. Executed side by side with the recommended expression (`review/evidence/r39-range.sh`):

| Scenario | py-shape | recommended | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| feature branch with upstream, leak on `HEAD` | blocks | blocks | `R1a`, `R1b` |
| `git push origin other` while on a clean `main` | **passes; the real push delivers the leaking branch to the remote** | blocks; remote lacks the ref | `R2a`, `R2d`, `R2e` vs `R2c`, `R2f`, `R2g` |
| new branch, no upstream (`@{u}` exits 128) | blocks via the `origin/HEAD` fallback | blocks | `R3a`–`R3c` |
| first push to an empty remote | **warns and exits 0** | blocks the real push | `R4a`, `R4b` vs `R4c`–`R4e` |
| detached `HEAD` | — | covered because `HEAD` is in the expression (0 commits without it, 1 with it) | `R7a`–`R7c` |
| a stash holding a token | — | not scanned (`refs/stash` is outside `--branches`/`--tags`) | `R6` |
| leak on a **different** unpushed branch, clean push | — | **blocks the clean push** | `R11a` |
| leak already pushed to a **second remote** (`fork`) with hooks bypassed, then `git push origin` | — | **passes; origin receives it** (0 commits scanned) | `R15a`–`R15c` |

The last row is the accepted cost: the flagged content is a real leak that has not been published, and the price buys a hook with no script and no stdin coupling. The stdin-exact form (`<local-sha> --not --remotes` per ref read from `githooks(5)` stdin) removes that over-scan (`R12a`) and still blocks the leaking branch (`R12b`, `R12c`); it is the ranked runner-up, chosen if R37's manager forwards pre-push stdin and the owner wants per-ref scoping. Residual gaps of the recommended form, neither of which py's shape or the stdin-exact runner-up closes: a push of an explicit object name that no branch, tag or `HEAD` reaches; and a commit already reachable from **any** remote-tracking ref, including a second remote such as a personal fork, is excluded even when the push targets a different remote (`R15b`, `R15c`; named by neither leg). Narrowing the exclusion to the destination remote, `--not --remotes=<remote>`, closes the second gap (`R15d`); git passes that remote's name to the `pre-push` hook as its first argument, so the narrowing is available only if R37's manager forwards hook arguments.

**The allowlist.** Every exemption is a blind spot, so the baseline ships none. The default global allowlist already covers the config file itself (`snapshots/gitleaks-default-config-v8.30.1.toml:25`, `SRC20b`) and other ecosystems' lockfiles; it has no `Cargo.lock` entry (`SRC20c`), and a real 592-line Rust lockfile produces no finding (`C6`). The commented example shows the narrow form for the first real false positive: `targetRules`, `condition = "AND"`, a fixture path and a value prefix together (`C7a`–`C7e`). Its prefix is `^fixture-`, not the `^test-only-` in Opus's example (`raw/opus.md:270`), because the default `generic-api-key` rule never flags a value beginning `test-only-` (`C7f`), so that example would exempt nothing. `.gitleaks.toml` as shipped (`review/evidence/proposed/gitleaks.toml`, sha256 `8dad313ef2f6f9f823a457d17bed43baaf9fe5d0674b0d16e5b018262e8a0443`):

```toml
# .gitleaks.toml — read by gitleaks >= 8.25 and by Betterleaks (legacy-format compatible).
title = "rs-launch-blueprint secret-scanning rules"

# Start from the scanner's maintained default rule set. It already ignores its own
# config file and the AWS documentation example keys (rule allowlist `.+EXAMPLE$`).
[extend]
useDefault = true

# No path or regex exemptions ship by default. Add one only for a real false positive,
# scoped as narrowly as possible, for example:
# [[allowlists]]
# description = "Fake credentials used by the web service's config-parsing tests"
# targetRules = ["generic-api-key"]
# condition = "AND"
# paths = ['''^crates/web/tests/fixtures/''']
# regexes = ['''^fixture-''']
```

The example's `crates/web/tests/fixtures/` path is illustrative; R02 owns the crate layout.

**The suppression file.** A fingerprint names one finding, so a new template has nothing to suppress. gitleaks prints two forms, and they behave differently (`review/evidence/r39-ignore.sh`):

| Form | Shape | Suppresses | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| path-form | `<path>:<rule-id>:<line>` | that path and line in every commit, at **both** tiers | `I1c`, `I2`, `I3c`; line-exact: `I5` |
| commit-form | `<commit-sha>:<path>:<rule-id>:<line>` | that one historical occurrence, at the range tier only | `I3b`, `I3d`; does not reach a re-staged copy: `I4a`, `I4b` |

```text
# .gitleaksignore — per-finding suppressions, one fingerprint per line.
# Pattern or path exemptions belong in .gitleaks.toml, not here.
#
# Prefer, in order:
#   1. an inline `gitleaks:allow` comment on a deliberate fake in a new change;
#   2. a commit-form fingerprint  <commit-sha>:<path>:<rule-id>:<line>  for a finding
#      already in history (it suppresses that one commit's occurrence only);
#   3. a path-form fingerprint   <path>:<rule-id>:<line>  only when (1) is impossible;
#      it suppresses that line in every commit and at both hook tiers.
# Precede every entry with a one-line comment saying what it is and why it is safe.
# To obtain a fingerprint:
#   gitleaks git --no-banner --redact --config .gitleaks.toml -v --log-opts="<range>" .
```
